He is a former professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Brisbane Bullets]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL). He played [[college basketball]] for [[California State University, Fresno|Fresno State]]. ==Early life== Johnson attended [[Saint Francis High School (Mountain View, California)|St. Francis High School]] in [[Mountain View, California]]. ==College career== In his four-year career at [[Fresno State Bulldogs men's basketball|Fresno State]], Johnson appeared in 127 games (87 starts) and averaged 10.6 points, 4.8 rebounds, 2.4 assists and 1.1 steals in 27.9 minutes per game while shooting 45.6 percent from the field, 37.4 percent from three-point range and 71.6 percent from the free-throw line. He finished his career ranked number 16 on Fresno State's all-time scoring list with 1,346 career points. As a senior, he was named to the All-[[Mountain West Conference]] second team and shot 43.2 percent from three-point range, the sixth-highest single-season three-point field goal percentage in school history.{{cite web|url=http://www.gobulldogs.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/tyler_johnson_734099.html|title=Tyler Johnson Bio|work=GoBulldogs.com|access-date=August 8, 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130907152411/http://www.gobulldogs.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/tyler_johnson_734099.html|archive-date=September 7, 2013}} ==Professional career== ===Sioux Falls Skyforce (2014–2015)=== After going undrafted in the [[2014 NBA draft]], Johnson joined the [[Miami Heat]] for the [[2014 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|title=HEAT Announce Summer League Information|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/heat-announce-summer-league-information-0|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=July 1, 2014|access-date=August 8, 2014}} On August 7, 2014, he signed with the Heat,{{cite web|title=HEAT Signs Tyler Johnson|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/heat/news/heat-signs-tyler-johnson_140807|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=August 7, 2014|access-date=August 8, 2014}} but was later waived by the team on October 25.{{cite web|title=HEAT Waive Birch, Drew, Johnson and Jones|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-waive-birch-drew-johnson-and-jones|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=October 25, 2014|access-date=October 25, 2014}} On November 3, he was acquired by the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] of the [[NBA Development League]] as an affiliate player of the Heat.{{cite web|title=Skyforce Announces Full Training Camp Roster|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=4890576|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=November 3, 2014|access-date=November 12, 2014}} === Miami Heat (2015) === On January 12, 2015, Johnson signed a 10-day contract with the Heat.{{cite web|title=HEAT Signs Tyler Johnson|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-signs-tyler-johnson-10-day|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=January 12, 2015|access-date=January 12, 2015}} Three days later, he made his NBA debut against the [[Golden State Warriors]], appearing for 1:44 minutes and scoring two points on a pair of free throws. === Return to the Skyforce (2015) === On January 22, the Heat decided to not retain Johnson after his contract expired{{cite web|first=Ira|last=Winderman|title=Heat part with Tyler Johnson after 10-day contract|url=http://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/miami-heat/sfl-miami-heat-tyler-johnson-s012215-story.html|work=Sun-Sentinel.com|date=January 22, 2015|access-date=January 23, 2015}} and two days later, he returned to the Skyforce.{{cite web|title=Tyler Johnson Returns to Skyforce|url=http://siouxfalls.dleague.nba.com/news/johnson-returns-to-skyforce/|work=NBA.com|date=January 24, 2015|access-date=January 26, 2015}} === Return to Miami (2015–2019) === Johnson later re-joined the Heat on January 29 as he signed another 10-day contract with the team.{{cite web|title=HEAT Signs Tyler Johnson to Second 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-signs-tyler-johnson-to-second-10-day-contract|work=NBA.com|date=January 29, 2015|access-date=January 29, 2015}} On February 8, he signed a two-year deal with the Heat.{{cite web|title=HEAT Signs Tyler Johnson For Remainder Of Season|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/heat-signs-tyler-johnson-remainder-season|work=NBA.com|date=February 8, 2015|access-date=February 8, 2015}}{{cite web|first=Shams|last=Charania|title=Tyler Johnson Signing Deal To Remain With Heat|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/236553/Tyler-Johnson-Signing-Deal-To-Remain-With-Heat|work=RealGM.com|date=February 8, 2015|access-date=February 8, 2015}} On March 2, he had a season-best game with 26 points and 4 steals in a 115–98 win over the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{cite web|title=Dragic scores 21, Heat beat Suns 115-98 as tensions run high|url=https://www.nba.com/games/20150302/PHXMIA/gameinfo.html|work=NBA.com|date=March 2, 2015|access-date=March 2, 2015}} Five days later, he scored 24 points and played in a career-high 44 minutes off the bench as he helped the Heat defeat the [[Sacramento Kings]], 114–109.{{cite web|title=Heat rally again and top Kings in OT, 114-109|url=https://www.nba.com/games/20150307/SACMIA/gameinfo.html|work=NBA.com|date=March 7, 2015|access-date=March 8, 2015}} He topped that minutes mark by playing in all 48 minutes of the Heat's season finale win over the Philadelphia 76ers.{{cite web|title=Tyler Johnson 2014-15 Game Log|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/j/johnsty01/gamelog/2015/|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=December 9, 2015}} On July 9, 2015, Johnson was sidelined for six weeks with a broken jaw that he sustained while playing for the Heat during the [[2015 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|title=Heat guard Tyler Johnson has broken jaw|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/heat-guard-tyler-johnson-broken-jaw-143418265--nba.html|work=Yahoo.com|date=July 9, 2015|access-date=July 9, 2015}} On December 9, 2015, he scored a season-high 20 points in a loss to the Charlotte Hornets.{{cite web|title=Hornets beat Heat 99-81 for third straight victory|url=https://www.nba.com/games/20151209/MIACHA/gameinfo.html|work=NBA.com|date=December 9, 2015|access-date=December 9, 2015}} He later missed eight games during December with a shoulder injury.{{cite web|title=Ellington's 7 3-pointers help Nets rally past Heat, 111-105|url=https://www.nba.com/games/20151228/BKNMIA/gameinfo.html|work=NBA.com|date=December 28, 2015|access-date=December 28, 2015}} Johnson fought through his left shoulder pain during January before missing the team's final two games of the month after succumbing to the pain.{{cite web|first=Ira|last=Winderman|title=Heat injury timetable remains uncertain with Whiteside, Tyler Johnson|url=http://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/miami-heat/sfl-miami-heat-hassan-whiteside-s013116-story.html|work=Sun-Sentinel.com|date=January 31, 2016|access-date=February 1, 2016}}{{cite web|first=Aric|last=Dilalla|title=Tyler Johnson out again, and surgery is still on the table|url=http://blogs.herald.com/miami_heat/2016/01/tyler-johnson-out-again-and-surgery-is-still-on-the-table.html|work=Herald.com|date=January 31, 2016|access-date=February 1, 2016}} After initially trying to avoid surgery, Johnson ultimately gave into the idea on February 1, 2016,{{cite web|title=Miami's Tyler Johnson will undergo surgery...|url=https://twitter.com/ShamsCharania/status/694228309018828801|work=Twitter|date=February 1, 2016|access-date=February 1, 2016}} a procedure that ruled him out for three months. He returned to action on May 1, coming off the bench for the final six minutes of the Heat's Game 7 win over the Charlotte Hornets in the first round of the playoffs. After the 2015–16 season, Johnson became a [[restricted free agent (NBA)|restricted free agent]]. On July 6, 2016, he received a four-year, $50 million offer sheet from the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web|title=Sources on @TheVertical: Miami RFA guard Tyler...|url=https://twitter.com/WojVerticalNBA/status/750936363030175744|work=Twitter|date=July 6, 2016|access-date=July 6, 2016}} Four days later, the Heat matched the Nets' contract offer, re-signing Johnson.{{cite web|title=HEAT Re-Signs Tyler Johnson|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-re-signs-tyler-johnson|work=NBA.com|date=July 10, 2016|access-date=July 10, 2016}} On December 7, 2016, he scored a career-high 27 points in a 103–95 loss to the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web|title=Hawks end 7-game skid behind Howard, Millsap|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899766|work=ESPN.com|date=December 7, 2016|access-date=December 8, 2016}} He topped that mark on December 20, scoring 32 points—the most any Heat reserve has ever scored in a game—in a 136–130 double overtime loss to the [[Orlando Magic]]. The previous Heat scoring record by a reserve was 29 points, by [[Voshon Lenard]] in 1999.{{cite web|title=Magic rally twice, then outlast Heat 136-130 in 2OT|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899864|work=ESPN.com|date=December 20, 2016|access-date=December 21, 2016}} On December 30, 2017, Johnson scored 22 of his season-high 31 points in the third quarter of the Heat's 117–111 win over the Magic.{{cite web|title=Johnson, Dragic lead Heat comeback in win over Magic|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975277|work=ESPN.com|date=December 30, 2017|access-date=December 30, 2017}} On December 23, 2018, Johnson scored 20 of his 25 points in the third quarter of the Heat's 115–91 win over the Magic.{{cite web|title=Heat beat Magic 115-91, Spoelstra gets 500th coaching win|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071172|work=ESPN.com|date=December 23, 2018|access-date=December 24, 2018}} ===Phoenix Suns (2019–2020)=== On February 6, 2019, Johnson was traded, along with [[Wayne Ellington]], to the [[Phoenix Suns]] in exchange for [[Ryan Anderson (basketball, born 1988)|Ryan Anderson]].{{cite web|title=Suns Acquire Tyler Johnson, Wayne Ellington from Miami|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-acquire-tyler-johnson-wayne-ellington-miami|work=NBA.com|date=February 6, 2019|access-date=February 6, 2019}} On February 23, he scored a season-high 29 points in a 120–112 loss to the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web|title=Young, Bazemore lead Hawks past Suns 120-112|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071556|work=ESPN.com|date=February 23, 2019|access-date=February 25, 2019}}{{cite web|title=Tyler Johnson 2018-19 Game Log|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/j/johnsty01/gamelog/2019/|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=February 25, 2019}} Two days later, he scored 18 points against his former team, the [[Miami Heat]], to help the Suns snap a franchise-record 17-game losing streak to win 124–121.{{cite web|title=Forty-point fourth quarter helps Suns snap 17-game slide|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071574|work=ESPN.com|date=February 25, 2019|access-date=February 25, 2019}} On April 4, 2019, Johnson was ruled out for the rest of the season after missing 10 games with right knee soreness and undergoing arthroscopic surgery.{{cite web|title=Suns' Tyler Johnson: Out for season|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/suns-tyler-johnson-out-for-season/|work=CBSSports.com|date=April 4, 2019|access-date=April 12, 2019}} On February 9, 2020, Johnson was waived by the Suns.{{cite web|title=Phoenix Suns waive guard Tyler Johnson|url=https://apnews.com/853ff520f7cb95e4468913f9f27701e7|work=APNews.com|date=February 10, 2019|access-date=February 10, 2019}}{{cite web|first=Brendon|last=Kleen|title=Report: Tyler Johnson waived just days after the NBA trade deadline|url=https://www.brightsideofthesun.com/2020/2/9/21130759/report-tyler-johnson-waived-after-nba-trade-deadline|website=BrightSideOfTheSun.com|date=February 9, 2020|access-date=June 25, 2020}} ===Brooklyn Nets (2020–2021)=== On June 24, 2020, Johnson signed with the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Tyler Johnson|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2020/06/24/brooklyn-nets-sign-tyler-johnson|website=NBA.com|date=June 24, 2020|access-date=June 25, 2020}} On November 27, he re-signed with the Nets.{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Re-Sign Tyler Johnson|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2020/11/27/brooklyn-nets-re-sign-tyler-johnson|website=NBA.com|date=November 27, 2020|access-date=November 27, 2020}} In 39 games played with Brooklyn, he averaged 5.4 points, 2 rebounds, and 1.2 assists in an average of 17 minutes per game. In the Nets' elimination from the NBA playoffs against the eventual champion Milwaukee Bucks, Johnson totalled 4 points, 2 rebounds, and 5 assists in a combined 22 minutes of action.{{cite web|title=Tyler Johnson, Basketball Player|url=https://www.proballers.com/basketball/player/65111/tyler-johnson|website=Proballers.com|access-date=November 17, 2021}} Johnson won praise for his personality fit and work with the Nets second unit, but Brooklyn chose not to re-sign him in free agency.{{cite web|title=Tyler Johnson played his role with the Brooklyn Nets|url=https://mwwire.com/2021/06/23/tyler-johnson-played-his-role-with-the-brooklyn-nets/|website=Mountain West Wire|date=June 23, 2021|access-date=November 17, 2021}} ===Philadelphia 76ers (2021–2022)=== On December 22, 2021, Johnson signed a 10-day contract with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]], via the hardship exemption.{{cite web|title=76ers Sign Tyler Johnson to 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/team-signs-tyler-johnson|website=NBA.com|date=December 22, 2021|access-date=December 22, 2021}} He appeared in three games and averaged 3.7 points and 2.0 rebounds per game. ===San Antonio Spurs (2022)=== On January 6, 2022, Johnson signed a 10-day contract with the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{Cite web|title=SPURS SIGN TYLER JOHNSON & ANTHONY LAMB TO 10-DAY CONTRACTS|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-sign-tyler-johnson-anthony-lamb-10-day-contracts|access-date=January 6, 2022|website=NBA.com|date=January 6, 2022}} He appeared in three games, and averaged 2 points, 2 rebounds, and 1.7 assists per game for the Spurs. ===Brisbane Bullets (2022–2023)=== On July 30, 2022, Johnson signed with the [[Brisbane Bullets]] in Australia for the [[2022–23 NBL season]].{{Cite web|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/bullets-add-exciting-import|title=Bullets Add "Exciting" Import|website=NBL.com.au|date=July 30, 2022|access-date=July 30, 2022}} ==Career
